summary.text: Ore is natural rock or sediment holding valuable minerals, often metals, concentrated above background levels and worth mining and processing.
Whether rock counts as ore comes down to weighing the value of the metals or minerals it holds against the cost of extracting them.
Mined ore is separated from unwanted gangue and then treated or refined, often by smelting, to recover the valuable metal or mineral.

facts.label: Complex ore
facts.value: Contains more than one valuable mineral

facts.label: Diamond source
facts.value: Kimberlites, from about 150 km down in the mantle

items.prompt: A rock body holds some copper, but digging it out and refining it would cost more than the copper is worth. Should it be called ore?

options.label: Yes, any rock with metal in it is ore
No, it is not worth mining
Yes, as long as the copper is pure
No, ore must contain more than one metal

items.explain: Ore must be economically viable: the value of what it holds has to outweigh the cost of extraction.

items.prompt: Two mines produce the same amount of metal, one from rich, high-grade rock and one from lower-grade rock. Which one piles up more tailings?
items.explain: Grade is the concentration of the wanted material, and tailings come in great quantity especially from lower-grade deposits.

items.prompt: Miners cannot avoid hauling up worthless rock mixed in with the valuable minerals. What is that unwanted material called?
items.explain: The part of an ore that is not economically desirable and cannot be avoided in mining is called gangue.

items.prompt: In mineral processing, what has to happen before the desired mineral can be concentrated?

options.label: The ore is freed from the gangue
The metal is smelted into bars
The deposit is given a name

items.explain: Processing starts with liberation, freeing the ore from the gangue, and then concentration separates out the desired mineral.

items.prompt: A company is prospecting for diamonds. Which kind of rock should it mainly look for?
items.explain: Kimberlites, which come up from deep in the mantle, are a primary source of diamonds.

items.prompt: Pegmatites are known for enormous crystals. What gives them such large crystals?

options.label: They cooled quickly at the surface
Water dissolved all the small crystals
They are made mostly of carbonates

items.explain: Pegmatites crystallize slowly at great depth beneath the surface, which leads to very large crystal sizes.
